settings.title: Settings
settings.notesFirst: Tap writes notes; hold places (old habit)
howto.title: How to play
howto.1: Every case has one solution. Each suspect, and the victim, stands on exactly one square.
howto.2: No two people share a row or a column. Crossed-out squares are blocked.
howto.3: Pick a suspect, then tap a square to place them. Tap them again to pick them up.
howto.4: Turn on Notes with Shift+N (or press and hold a square) to pencil in maybes and rule squares out.
howto.5: When everyone is placed, look at the victim's room: exactly one other person is in it, alone with the victim. That's the murderer. Other rooms can hold any number of people.
hint.misplaced.1: Something on the board doesn't add up yet.
hint.misplaced.3a: {name} can't be at {cell}: statement {n} rules it out.
hint.misplaced.3b: {name} isn't at {cell}. Something else has to give.
hint.next.1: Try {name} next. Their statement narrows it down.
hint.verdict.1: Everyone is in the right place. Who shares {victim}'s room?
hint.verdict.2: Look only at the {room}: exactly one other person is in it.
hint.verdict.cell: Everyone is in the right place. Close the case.
library.training: New here? Start with the training case
coach.intro: Welcome, detective! Everyone here, the victim too, stood on one square, and no two people share a row or a column. Read the statements and place everyone. Then look at the victim's room: the one other person in it was alone with the victim. Other rooms can hold any number of people.
coach.pick: Let's start with {name}. Tap {name}'s card to pick them.
coach.first: {name} says: “{statement}” Only one square on the board fits. It's highlighted: tap it.
coach.single: {name} says: “{statement}” Taken rows and columns are crossed out, so only the highlighted square is left. Tap it.
coach.narrow: {name} says: “{statement}” The highlighted squares still fit. Which one does the statement allow?
coach.wrong: Hmm, {name} can't be at {cell}. Tap them to pick them up and look again.
coach.verdict: Everyone is in place! The highlighted room is {victim}'s, and exactly one other person is in it: they were alone with {victim}. Other rooms can hold several people; only this room counts. Press “Name the murderer” and pick them.
coach.close: Everyone is in place! Press “Close the case”.
coach.done: Case closed: you're a detective now. A new case is waiting in the case files.
coach.silent: {name} has no statement, but every other row and column is taken. Only the highlighted square is left: tap it.

library.headline: More mysteries. Worth solving.
library.intro: We build puzzles around the pleasure of figuring things out: a way in, clues that connect, and a discovery that changes the picture.
library.collectionBody: Choose a world and a challenge. Each case has its own map, clues and checked solution.
library.noMatches: No cases match these choices. Try another setting or size.
library.classicsBody: Explore the original casebook, including the 24 × 24 Museum. Settle in for a longer investigation.
library.dailyBody: A shared case to come back to each day. There is always the collection to explore between visits.
library.trainingBody: Our guided case walks you through the clues, one discovery at a time.

workshop.storyTitle: We wanted more good puzzles to play.
workshop.storyBody: After tackling the official Treasure Hunt, we built a workshop to keep making mysteries. Explore the generator, the deductions behind the puzzles, and our work toward cases that stay interesting.
